items.claim: The span 7:1-7:6 is a sound unit and its medium_low grade is honest, but one reference line places the weak connective of 7:1 at word 12, while the witness line for oshb:Dan.7.1 has בֵּאדַ֨יִן֙ as its token 13 of 18; the word-position convention of the language-zone layer is the split-token one (it ends the Aramaic run at Dan.7.28 w16, and the witness line for 7:28 has 16 tokens). items.both_sides: Onset 6:28/7:1 (web:Dan.6.28 = oshb:Dan.6.29): the far side is a narrator's regnal notice followed by a petuchah (WLC only); the near side is one of the inventory's eight datelines, with a restart of the regnal sequence. Strong on both sides; I propose no cut. Close 7:6/7:7: the close side ends the third beast on a grant of dominion; the onset side carries the long seeing formula with the night-visions phrase, which the inventory finds in this chapter at 7:2, 7:7 and 7:13 only. Against it, the after-this connective stands at both 7:6 and 7:7, and the four beasts are announced as one set at 7:3. The row weighs both and grades the edge medium_low; I agree.

items.claim: 7:7-7:12 holds one movement: the fourth beast and its horn (7:7-7:8), the court (7:9-7:10) and the sentence carried out on the beasts (7:11-7:12). The court verses do not stand free of the beast series, because 7:11 names the horn's words again and 7:12 settles the other beasts. medium_low is the right grade, set by the onset at 7:6/7:7.
items.both_sides: Onset 7:6/7:7: as weighed under the row before it; long formula on the onset side, a shared after-this connective on both. Against the close: the Ancient of Days stands on both sides (7:9 and 7:13) and the dominion removed at 7:12 is the dominion granted at 7:14, so the court scene runs on. The row names that rival under the next row and grades this edge medium; I agree. I propose no cut.

A finished question-and-answer pair stands before the seam and a new question after it, so the edge is better than the one at 7:22/7:23, which parts a question from its own answer. I propose no cut.

triage_answers.decision: Yes for all seven rows: each listed field holds at least one claim or count with no tier word. Every such claim that names a layer is true of that layer, so the fault is the missing word and not a false statement. W4-001 strongest_rejected_alternative: which verses carry the long and the short seeing formula (the inventory holds it; EXTRACTED is the true word) and the weighing 'better-attested step' (INFERRED). W4-001 device_notes: K/Q at 7:5 and 7:6 and 'wholly Aramaic' name their layers without a tier word (EXTRACTED is true of both); the third-person frame and first-person report is a reading of the witness (INFERRED). W4-002 strongest_rejected_alternative: 7:11 resumes the horn and 7:11-7:12 resolve the series (INFERRED). W4-003 boundary_rationale: the device facts at 7:13, 7:14, 7:15 and the petuchah after 7:14 name layers without a tier word (EXTRACTED is true), and 'signals on both sides' is a weighing (INFERRED). W4-004 strongest_rejected_alternative: the plan lists 7:15-7:16 as a turn (EXTRACTED from the plan is true) and 'would be an over-split' (INFERRED). W4-005 strongest_rejected_alternative: nine verses (correct), 7:22 closes on the kingdom clause, 7:23 changes speaker (witness facts; EXTRACTED) and the weighing (INFERRED). W4-006 strongest_rejected_alternative: 7:26 opens with a conjunction, and no refrain or speaker change at 7:25/7:26, a negative range claim (true of the witness; it owes a tier). W4-007 strongest_rejected_alternative: six verses (correct), 7:28 changes speaker (witness fact), and the weighing (INFERRED). Severity low throughout.
